weather: Showers over south-east England and the Channel, with steady rain across the rest of the country.
air: Convoy CW 3, code name Bread, was attacked off Dover in the early afternoon by about 26 Do 17s of KG 2 escorted by Bf 110s and Bf 109s. Hurricanes and Spitfires of 32, 56, 64, 74 and 111 Squadrons engaged and only one small ship was sunk. A Hurricane of 111 Squadron was lost after colliding with a Dornier. Other bombers hit shipping at Falmouth and a factory at Swansea.
home: The British Union of Fascists was declared an unlawful organisation on 10 July.
Tea went on the ration this week at 2 ounces per person per week.
The French National Assembly at Vichy voted 569 to 80 on 10 July to give full powers to Marshal Pétain.
reich: U-34 sank the Finnish steamer Petsamo and U-61 sank the Dutch steamer Alwaki on 10 July.
An OKW order signed by Keitel on 10 July called for heavy coastal batteries between Calais and Boulogne to cover a Channel crossing.
Hitler received the Hungarian Prime Minister, Count Teleki, on 10 July.

weather: Overcast over the Channel with cloud base near 5,000 feet and fair visibility, thunderstorms and bright intervals further north.
air: Ju 87s of StG 2 attacked shipping off Portland in the morning and sank the armed yacht HMS Warrior II, and 501 and 609 Squadrons lost three fighters to the escort. A second raid bombed Portland harbour just before noon, and the escorting Bf 110s of ZG 76 lost four aircraft to Hurricanes. He 111s raided Portsmouth in the early evening. A convoy off Suffolk was attacked without loss.
home: Mr R. A. Butler told the Commons on 11 July that Britain would treat Haile Selassie's Ethiopian government as an ally.
Lord Beaverbrook, Minister of Aircraft Production, appealed this week for household aluminium to be given for aircraft manufacture.
Marshal Pétain issued constitutional acts on 11 July abolishing the office of President of the French Republic.
reich: U-34 sank the Norwegian steamer Janna from convoy HX 54 on 11 July.
Grand Admiral Raeder reported to Hitler at the Berghof on 11 July and advised that a landing in England be treated as a last resort.
Romania withdrew from the League of Nations on 11 July.

weather: Mostly cloudy with early fog in the Channel and thunderstorms in many districts.
air: He 111s and Do 17s attacked convoy Booty off the Essex and Suffolk coast during the morning and were met by Hurricanes of 17, 85, 151 and 242 Squadrons. He 111s of KG 26 bombed Aberdeen at midday, killing 29 people, and 603 Squadron shot one down. Other raiders were engaged off the Isle of Wight and near Portsmouth. Bombs fell in South Wales during the night.
home: Aberdeen was bombed at midday on 12 July and 29 people were killed.
Pierre Laval was appointed Vice Premier of the French government at Vichy on 12 July.
reich: U-99 under Otto Kretschmer sank the Greek steamer Ia on 12 July and captured the Estonian steamer Merisaar.
General Jodl of the OKW wrote a memorandum on 12 July describing a landing in England as a river crossing on a broad front.

weather: Early fog over southern England cleared by the middle of the morning.
air: Shipping off Portland and Dover was the main target. Hurricanes of 238 Squadron and Spitfires of 609 Squadron met about 50 German aircraft off Portland, including Bf 110s of V./LG 1. In the late afternoon Ju 87s of StG 1 with JG 51 escort attacked a convoy off Dover and fought 56, 54 and 64 Squadrons. The destroyer HMS Vanessa was disabled by a near miss and towed into Dover.
home: Italian forces crossed from Ethiopia into Kenya on 13 July and attacked the British garrison at Moyale.
No. 302 Squadron, the first Polish fighter squadron in the RAF, was formed at Leconfield on 13 July.
reich: Hitler met Brauchitsch and Halder at the Berghof on 13 July to hear the Army's plans for a landing in England.

weather: Fair all day.
air: More than 40 Ju 87s of IV.(St)/LG 1 with Bf 109 escort attacked a convoy off Dover in the afternoon and were engaged by 151, 610 and 615 Squadrons. The coaster Island Queen was hit and later sank, and two other ships were damaged. BBC reporter Charles Gardner recorded a commentary on the fight from the cliffs. Pilot Officer Mudie of 615 Squadron was shot down and died the next day.
home: Mr Churchill said in a broadcast on the evening of 14 July that Britain would seek no terms and tolerate no parley.
General de Gaulle reviewed Free French troops in London on 14 July and laid a wreath at the statue of Marshal Foch.
The Air Ministry stated on 14 July that German ambulance seaplanes found near British shipping would fly at their own risk.
reich: U-52 sank the Greek steamer Thetis A. and the submarine UA sank the Norwegian ship Sarita on 14 July.

weather: Low cloud and worsening conditions over the Channel and southern England restricted flying.
air: Poor weather limited operations. Fifteen Do 17s of KG 2 attacked convoy Pilot in the early afternoon and were met by Hurricanes of 56 and 151 Squadrons. Single raiders bombed the Westland works at Yeovil, St Athan airfield and the Kemp Town district of Brighton. Spitfires of 603 Squadron shot down an He 111 off Peterhead.
home: British troops withdrew from Moyale on the Kenya frontier on 15 July.
Results were announced on 15 July for the Soviet-run elections in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
reich: U-34 sank the Greek steamer Evdoxia on 15 July.
Germany moved its customs frontier on 15 July to the pre-1914 border, bringing Alsace and Lorraine inside the German customs area.

weather: Fog over northern France, the Straits of Dover and south-east England.
air: Fog kept activity low. In the afternoon Spitfires of 603 Squadron shot down an He 111 of KG 26 off Fraserburgh. Hurricanes of 601 Squadron intercepted Ju 88s of KG 54 and shot one down into the Solent. Night activity was mainly minelaying off the east coast.
home: The Japanese cabinet of Admiral Yonai resigned on 16 July.
The Democratic National Convention opened in Chicago on 15 July.
reich: Hitler signed Directive No. 16 on 16 July, ordering preparations for a landing operation against England.
U-61 sank the British ship Scottish Minstrel from convoy HX 55 on 16 July.

weather: Dull with occasional rain.
air: Weather again restricted flying. German aircraft searched for shipping off Scotland and the east coast. An He 111 of KG 26 and a Ju 88 of KG 51 were shot down, and a Spitfire of 64 Squadron was lost with its pilot wounded. At night bombs fell in South Wales and around the Thames Estuary while minelaying continued.
home: Britain agreed on 17 July to close the Burma Road supply route to China for three months.
reich: U-57 sank the British steamer Manipur and the Swedish steamer O.A. Brodin on 17 July, and U-43 sank the British steamer Fellside.
Grand Admiral Raeder and Field Marshal von Brauchitsch conferred on 17 July about the planned landing in England.

weather: Occasional rain in the south, cloudy over the Straits of Dover, and cool.
air: Shipping off the south and east coasts was attacked and the East Goodwin lightship was bombed and sunk. 609 Squadron lost two Spitfires to Ju 88s off Swanage, and a 610 Squadron Spitfire was shot down by Bf 109s near Calais. Bombs fell on Montrose airfield and St Athan. In the evening nine Blenheims bombed Boulogne.
home: Vichy French aircraft bombed Gibraltar on 18 July in reprisal for the British attack at Mers el Kébir.
President Roosevelt was nominated for a third term by the Democratic convention in Chicago on 18 July.
RAF Bomber Command raided the Krupp works at Essen and targets at Bremen and Hamm on the night of 18 July.
reich: Troops returning from the campaign in France paraded through the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin on 18 July.
U-99 sank the British steamer Woodbury and U-58 sank the Norwegian steamer Gyda on 18 July.

weather: Showers with bright intervals, fair over the Channel with light winds.
air: Nine Defiants of 141 Squadron on patrol off Folkestone were attacked by Bf 109s of III./JG 51 shortly after midday. Five were shot down and a sixth was written off, with heavy loss of life, before Hurricanes of 111 Squadron intervened. In the afternoon Do 17s and Ju 87s bombed Dover harbour, where the oiler War Sepoy blew up and the destroyer HMS Griffin was damaged.
home: General Sir Alan Brooke was appointed Commander in Chief, Home Forces, on 19 July.
HMAS Sydney and British destroyers sank the Italian cruiser Bartolomeo Colleoni off Cape Spada, Crete, on 19 July.
President Roosevelt accepted nomination for a third term on 19 July.
reich: Hitler addressed the Reichstag at the Kroll Opera House on 19 July and made what he called an appeal to reason directed at Britain.
At the same session Göring was promoted to Reichsmarschall and twelve generals were made field marshals.
U-62 sank the British steamer Pearlmoor from convoy SL 38 on 19 July.

weather: Occasional thunderstorms, with cloud over the Straits of Dover clearing to bright intervals.
air: Convoy Bosom was the main target as it moved east along the south coast. Around 18:00 Ju 87s of II./StG 1, escorted by Bf 109s of JG 27 and JG 51, attacked it off Dover and were met by 32, 615, 65 and 610 Squadrons. The coaster Pulborough was sunk and the destroyer HMS Brazen was hit and later sank. Two He 59 rescue seaplanes were also shot down during the day.
home: The government banned the buying and selling of new cars from 20 July.
Hitler's Reichstag speech of 19 July was rejected the same evening in an unofficial BBC German broadcast by Sefton Delmer.
reich: Ju 87 dive bombers sank the British destroyer Brazen off Dover on 20 July.
An Fw 200 Condor of KG 40 was lost over north-east England on the night of 19 to 20 July.

weather: Fine early, cloud building during the morning, fair again by evening.
air: Standing patrols covered westbound convoy CW 7 through the Straits of Dover and along the south coast. Off the Needles, 43 and 238 Squadrons met Do 17s escorted by about 50 Bf 109s and Bf 110s, and a 43 Squadron Hurricane collided with a Bf 109, killing both pilots. 238 Squadron also shot down a Do 17 and a Bf 110.
home: Britain recognised the Czechoslovak provisional government of Dr Benes in London on 21 July.
The new parliaments of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania voted on 21 July to ask for admission to the Soviet Union.
reich: Hitler conferred with the heads of the armed services in Berlin on 21 July about a landing in England, which he called an exceptionally daring undertaking.
Göring met his senior Luftwaffe commanders at Carinhall on 21 July to discuss the air war against the RAF.
U-30 sank the British steamer Ellaroy on 21 July.

weather: Fair in the Straits, cloudy in the Channel, light westerly winds, with showers and bright intervals in the east.
air: A quiet day. Hurricanes of 145 Squadron shot down a reconnaissance Do 17 off Selsey Bill in the morning, and convoys off the east coast were attacked. Bombs on the prisoner of war camp at Duff House, Banff, killed six German prisoners. In the night of 22 to 23 July a Blenheim of the Fighter Interception Unit shot down a Do 17 off Sussex, the first success with airborne radar.
home: Lord Halifax, the Foreign Secretary, rejected Hitler's peace offer in a broadcast on the evening of 22 July.
Prince Konoye became Prime Minister of Japan on 22 July.
reich: The British Foreign Secretary, Lord Halifax, rejected the offer made in the Reichstag speech in a broadcast on 22 July.
Work began on 22 July on emplacing heavy coastal guns on the French Channel coast.

weather: Slight haze in the Straits of Dover, cloudy with occasional rain elsewhere.
air: Activity was light. Convoys off Yarmouth and Lowestoft were approached in the morning, trawlers were bombed off North Foreland and bombs fell near Pulham in Norfolk in the afternoon. A Ju 88 was shot down by 242 Squadron near Great Yarmouth. At night minelaying ran from Dover to the Forth and an He 111 was shot down near Dunbar.
home: Sir Kingsley Wood's budget of 23 July raised the standard rate of income tax to 8s 6d in the pound.
The Local Defence Volunteers were officially renamed the Home Guard on 23 July.
reich: The United States declared on 23 July that it would not recognise the Soviet annexation of the Baltic states.

weather: Cloudy over the Channel and Straits, coastal and hill fog in the west spreading east, rain in most districts.
air: Do 17s attacked convoys in the Straits of Dover and the Thames Estuary during the morning. Spitfires of 54, 65 and 610 Squadrons fought Bf 109s of JG 26 and JG 52 over Margate, and 54 Squadron lost two aircraft. A Ju 88 of KG 51 that attacked shipping in the Bristol Channel was shot down by 92 and 87 Squadrons. A lone Ju 88 bombed the Brooklands area in the afternoon.
home: Lord Beaverbrook thanked the public in a broadcast on 24 July for their part in fighter production.
The French liner Meknès, taking French naval personnel home, was torpedoed in the Channel on the night of 24 July and 416 died.
reich: The motor torpedo boat S 27 sank the French liner Meknès in the Channel on 24 July.
The submarine U-139 was commissioned on 24 July.

weather: Fine with haze in the Straits of Dover and light north-westerly winds.
air: Convoy CW 8 of 21 ships was attacked repeatedly in the Dover Straits and off Folkestone by Ju 87s and Ju 88s under heavy Bf 109 escort. Five merchant ships were sunk by air attack and the destroyers Boreas and Brilliant were damaged. Squadrons engaged included 32, 54, 64, 65, 111, 610 and 615. E-boats attacked the remaining ships that night.
home: Women and children were ordered on 25 July to leave Gibraltar.
reich: Economics Minister Walther Funk set out plans for the economic reorganisation of Europe in a speech on 25 July.
Grand Admiral Raeder told Hitler on 25 July that the Navy could not be ready for a landing before the middle of September.

weather: Heavy cloud, rain and poor visibility.
air: Poor weather kept activity down. Raids approaching Swanage, Portland and the Isle of Wight mostly turned back when fighters appeared, and 601 Squadron lost a Hurricane off the Isle of Wight. E-boats sank three ships of convoy CW 8, and the Admiralty stopped daylight merchant sailings through the Dover Strait. After midnight a Hurricane of 87 Squadron shot down an He 111 engaged in minelaying.
home: The United States placed exports of aviation fuel and some grades of scrap metal to Japan under licence on 26 July.
reich: Hitler received the Romanian Prime Minister Gigurtu and Foreign Minister Manoilescu at the Berghof on 26 July.
U-34 sank the British liner Accra and the steamer Vinemoor from convoy OB 188 on 26 July.

weather: Fair in the Straits, cloudy in the Channel, slight rain in the Midlands and over the North Sea.
air: Ju 87s with Bf 109 escort attacked a convoy off Swanage in the morning. He 111s of KG 53 sank the destroyer HMS Wren off Aldeburgh and damaged HMS Montrose. Dover harbour was raided twice in the afternoon, the destroyer leader HMS Codrington was sunk at her moorings and HMS Walpole was damaged. The Admiralty then gave up Dover as a destroyer base.
home: Japanese police arrested a number of British residents on 27 July, among them the Reuters correspondent Melville Cox.
reich: German bombers sank the British destroyers Codrington at Dover and Wren off Aldeburgh on 27 July.
U-34 sank the British ships Thiara and Sambre from convoy OB 188 on 27 July.

weather: Fine early and fair for the rest of the day, clouding over in the evening.
air: At dawn 234 Squadron shot down a Ju 88 near Plymouth. A large raid approached Dover in the early afternoon and turned away without bombing. Spitfires of 74 and 41 Squadrons fought the Bf 109 escort of JG 51, whose commander Major Werner Mölders was wounded and force landed in France. Hurricanes of 111 Squadron shot down two He 59 rescue seaplanes off Boulogne.
home: A Ju 88 came down almost undamaged near Bexhill early on 28 July and its crew was captured.
reich: Hitler received President Tiso, Prime Minister Tuka and Alexander Mach of Slovakia at the Berghof on 28 July.
Major Werner Mölders, commander of JG 51, was wounded in combat over the Channel on 28 July.
U-99 sank the British ship Auckland Star on 28 July.

weather: Fair over the whole country, hazy in the Thames Estuary and at Dover.
air: About 40 Ju 87s with some 50 Bf 109s raided Dover harbour at about 07:30 and were engaged by 41 and 501 Squadrons among others. The steamer Gronland and the yacht Gulzar were sunk and the depot ship Sandhurst was set on fire. Ju 88s attacked shipping off Dungeness and Bf 110s went for a convoy off the east coast. In the evening Ju 87s of StG 2 sank the destroyer HMS Delight off Portland.
home: Melville Cox of Reuters died on 29 July after a fall from a window while held by the Japanese military police in Tokyo.
reich: A Naval Staff memorandum of 29 July judged a mid-September landing possible but recommended postponing it to May 1941.
Dive bombers sank the British destroyer Delight off Portland on 29 July.
U-99 sank the British steamer Clan Menzies on 29 July.

weather: Unsettled with low cloud and drizzle.
air: Weather kept activity low. Raids approached convoys off Orfordness, Clacton and Harwich, and 85 Squadron shot down a Bf 110 off the Suffolk coast. Spitfires of 603 Squadron shot down an He 111 of KG 26 near Montrose. At night bombs fell in Surrey, South Wales and the Bristol area.
home: Mr Eden told the Commons on 30 July that the Home Guard would be issued with army boots as supplies allowed.
reich: Hitler instructed Göring on 30 July to prepare the Luftwaffe for a large scale air offensive against Britain.
The Naval Staff reported to the OKW on 30 July on the state of preparations for a landing in England.

weather: Fair across the country with temperatures a little above average, haze in the Channel and Straits.
air: Haze limited operations to reconnaissance and small shipping raids off the south and east coasts. At about 16:00 Bf 109s of JG 2 attacked the Dover balloon barrage and were engaged by Spitfires of 74 Squadron, which lost two pilots killed, Pilot Officer Gunn and Sergeant Eley. At night raiders from the Cherbourg area bombed South Wales and the Thames Estuary area.
home: Twenty-one American republics signed the Act of Havana on 30 July, covering European possessions in the Americas.
Vichy France decreed on 31 July the death penalty for French servicemen who join a foreign army.
reich: Hitler met Keitel, Jodl, Raeder, Brauchitsch and Halder at the Berghof on 31 July, where Raeder said the Navy could not be ready before mid-September.
U-99 sank the British steamers Jamaica Progress and Jersey City on 31 July.
